traps.shape: a DAST/fuzz payload and each value of the fuzz input map are rendered again, so a value taken from the target's response is evaluated as template source
traps.realistic_because: the route the advisory describes; the second render reads as interactsh bookkeeping and the value map looks like CLI variables

traps.pattern: A (far site, shared evaluator; how-type shape trap)
traps.shape: a target-derived value is substituted raw into a template-authored expression's string literal before that expression is compiled, so quotes in the value change the expression
traps.realistic_because: ordinary response chaining that every template relies on; the value only matters when the author placed a placeholder inside a helper's quoted argument, so a plain rendering check looks sufficient

traps.shape: a matcher resolves placeholders and compiles the resulting text, so a response-derived value becomes part of the matcher expression and can force a match
traps.realistic_because: the expression is template-authored and the value appears only inside an already-quoted literal, so it reads as matcher semantics rather than the disclosure path

traps.shape: a value supplied at scan time that shadows a declared template variable is rendered instead of used as data
traps.realistic_because: declared variables are legitimately overridable, so the merge reads as precedence handling; removing the override would break the coupled functional behaviour

traps.pattern: B (route where the protection never existed)
traps.shape: the shared placeholder renderer substitutes one marker form and then runs the other form over the first pass's output, so a target-derived value carrying the legacy form is resolved
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the legacy form has its own pre-existing pass, the published fix never touches the file, and current upstream still has the two-pass implementation

traps.shape: a DSL extractor resolves placeholders and compiles the resulting text, so a response-derived value used inside an extractor expression becomes expression source
traps.realistic_because: feature parity with the matcher's placeholder support; extraction is output-side, and the expression is template-authored with the value inside a quoted literal

traps.shape: extracted values are expanded as template source before they are reported, so a response-derived value names an expression that is evaluated into the result
traps.realistic_because: a report-side convenience expansion; the values are already extraction results, so they look like final data rather than template text
